QF.id: IV Clearing Settlement and Risk Management_34

question.text: What is the settlement cycle for daily MTM in exchange-traded interest rate derivatives?

answer.text: T+1 basis (settlement on the next business day after the trade day)
T+2 basis (two business days after the trade)

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the ETIRD workbook (pp.227, 240), daily MTM settlement for exchange-traded interest rate derivatives is cash settled through clearing accounts on T+1 — calculated at end of day T and settled on the next business day per the clearing corporation timeline. The Trap: While MTM is calculated daily, the actual fund transfer happens on T+1, not the same day. Weekly settlement does not apply to exchange-traded derivatives. Note: Focus on the ETIRD-specific T+1 timeline stated in the workbook; do not generalize from other market segments unless those are separately sourced.
